headline: Low interaction risk overall: pdf.js is browser-based and Taipy has no documented write or egress surfaces, so pairwise harms are limited and mostly require unusual integration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js can render attacker-controlled PDF content in a browser-based workflow, while Taipy has no documented ingestion path from pdf.js outputs. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not default, but if an operator manually copies rendered text or exports from pdf.js into Taipy, malicious document content could influence downstream instructions.
conditions: IF an operator copies PDF-derived text from pdf.js into Taipy inputs without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF Taipy is configured to treat imported text as instructions, malicious PDF content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Use a manual review step before pasting PDF text into Taipy.
Strip instructions and markup from extracted PDF text.
Keep pdf.js outputs in read-only review mode.
Add a prompt firewall for any text imported into Taipy.
requires-engineering: build provenance tagging from pdf.js to Taipy.

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents, but its network egress is none; Taipy also shows no network egress and no declared data classes. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, leakage between them is not a default pathway. Residual risk exists only if the operator moves sensitive PDFs into a shared location or exports content manually.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder containing sensitive PDFs, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is later configured to upload file contents, the pair can expose document contents.
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs in separate folders per tool.
Disable any export or sync step between the tools.
Review Taipy inputs before loading document-derived data.
Use local-only storage for intermediate files.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and file handling for PDFs, while Taipy is a data-engineering app with no documented write surfaces or concurrency model here. Because overlapping mutable resources are not shown, direct write conflict is not default. Uncertainty remains about hidden shared state, so the safer low rating is used.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same files or directories, conflicts become possible.
IF Taipy is given a mutable shared resource not listed in its profile, contention risk rises.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use read-only mounts for pdf.js outputs.
Check Taipy for any hidden write targets before deployment.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted or rendered document content, and Taipy may consume data-engineering inputs, but neither profile shows an automatic trust chain. Without evidence that Taipy treats pdf.js output as authoritative, cascading error is limited to manual pipelines and can be interrupted by review.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is fed into Taipy without validation, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Taipy automates actions from imported document data, bad PDF extraction can cascade.
mitigations: Validate extracted fields before Taipy ingestion.
Require human approval for any action derived from PDF content.
Compare extracted text against the source PDF.
Log provenance for each imported record.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in either profile: pdf.js is open-source document processing with no declared residency or retention constraints, and Taipy likewise exposes no residency, certification, or retention obligations here. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, a pairwise compliance breach is not provable from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data with external residency or retention requirements, reassess compliance.
IF deployment policies add logging or export of sensitive documents, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Document the data classes each tool may handle.
Review deployment residency requirements before use.
Keep regulated data out of both tools until policies are defined.
Add retention settings if sensitive documents are introduced.
requires-engineering: map each tool to a formal compliance control set.
